newsitem.title: USA: Stocks scratch out modest gains after rally fizzles.
newsitem.headline: Stocks scratch out modest gains after rally fizzles.

text.p: Stocks closed slightly higher on Thursday, but for the second straight session, a sharp run-up evaporated as the market again consolidated its steep, summer-long rally.
The Dow Jones industrial average ended up 13.71 points at 7,942.03. The blue-chip index has soared nearly 880 points so far this summer on the back of moderate economic growth and subdued inflation.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,516 to 1,258 on heavy volume of 530 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
Stocks got some support for the bond market, which rallied after the government reported the Consumer Price Index rose a mere 0.2 percent in July, in line with forecasts.
The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond was up nearly a full point, which lowered its yield to 6.55 percent from Wednesday's close of 6.63 percent.

Despite the retreat in bond interest rates from a recent peak of 6.70 percent, the stock market still felt that the long-bond yield was still high. The rate is one-quarter point higher than the 6.33 percent on July 30, when the Dow stood at a then record 8,254.89.
Analysts said investors clearly remained on edge, selling stocks into any market strength as rates remained well higher than a week ago.

"There were great expectations built into the (stock) market then," said Dick Stein, vice president at U.S. Clearing Corp. "Just last week, people were talking about interest rates going to 6 percent."
Stocks mirrored Wednesday's pattern, as the market burst higher at the open in relief over tame inflation data, only to sharply reverse course later in the session.

With their interest rate wish list evidently on hold, investors displayed an edgy willingness to sell into any market strength, analysts said, and stocks continued to work through a choppy consolidation.

"This is the kind of consolidation that has to go on after a significant run-up," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd. "We went through a long period where there were just no down days."
"With rates at 6.50 percent or below, valuations had some room to grow," he said, "but above 6.50 and they start to look a little stretched."

Among individual issues, Columbia/HCA Healthcare Corp. fell 1-7/16 to 31-5/16 on growing Wall Street concern the federal probe of the company's Medicare billings could implicate senior executives in the organization.
Kmart Corp. rose 1-1/8 to 12-7/8 after the discount chain store became the latest retailer to report strong quarterly earnings.

Uniforce Services Inc. jumped 6-1/2 to 29-15/16 after it agreed to accept a $32 per share cash and stock acquisition bid from fellow staffing service company Comforce Corp. Comforce fell 1/2 to 7-1/2.

Talbert Medical Management Holdings Corp. gained 5-3/8 to 62-3/8. Talbert, a physician practice management company, agreed to be acquired by MedPartners Inc. for $63 per share in cash. MedPartners rose 7/16 to 22-15/16.
The Nasdaq Composite index gained 3.29 points to 1,586.69.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks rose 2.75 to 924.77. The American Stock Exchange index slipped 0.67 to 640.39.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks rose 1.24 to 479.66. The average share was up 11 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 8,807.287, up 22.518 or 0.26 percent.
